nandi-monsoon.alt: Monsoon cloud rolling over the green flank of the Nandi Hills, with the plateau spread out below.
nandi-monsoon.caption: The plateau north of Bengaluru in the monsoon, from the Nandi Hills.
nandi-monsoon.author: Harsha K R

red-earth-path.alt: A freshly cut red-earth path running beside the water of Jakkur Lake, with date palms and scrub.
red-earth-path.caption: Red earth beside Jakkur Lake, North Bengaluru.
red-earth-path.author: Shankar Raman

plateau-hill.alt: A lone granite hill rising from the hazy blue plateau under a clear sky.
plateau-hill.caption: A granite hill on the plateau, seen from the Nandi Hills area.
plateau-hill.author: Lijith.l7

raintree-canopy.alt: Looking up into the wide, branching canopy of a rain tree.
raintree-canopy.caption: Under a rain tree (Samanea saman), Mysuru — the species planned for the valley.
raintree-canopy.author: Vinayaraj

jakkur-lake.alt: Wide view of Jakkur Lake in early morning light, with a bund path, coconut palms and distant towers.
jakkur-lake.caption: Jakkur Lake, one of the tanks of North Bengaluru, early morning.
jakkur-lake.author: Manu.mohan

nandydroog-1790s.alt: Hand-coloured engraving of the granite fort hill of Nandidurg rising above a rocky plain.
nandydroog-1790s.caption: N.W. view of Nandydroog, from Colebrooke’s Twelve Views of Places in the Kingdom of Mysore, published 1805.
nandydroog-1790s.author: J. W. Edy after R. H. Colebrooke

hebbal-lake.alt: Hebbal Lake on a hazy morning: still water dotted with birds, a low island of scrub, a line of stones and faint towers on the far shore.
hebbal-lake.caption: Hebbal Lake, one of the old tanks on the northern edge of Bengaluru, on a February morning in 2008.
hebbal-lake.author: Nagesh Kamath
